classification.difficultyReason: Interpret the semi-vertical angle to obtain r=h and distinguish horizontal water-surface area from wetted lateral area before connecting each rate to volume inflow.

content.prompt: An upturned cone of semi-vertical angle $45^\circ$ is being filled with water at a constant rate of $20\text{ cm}^3/\text{s}$. Find the rate at which the height of the water, the area of the water surface, and the area of the cone wetted by the water, are increasing when the water height is $50\text{ cm}$.

answer.short: Height: $\dfrac{4}{125\pi}\text{ cm/s}$; water surface area: $\dfrac45\text{ cm}^2/\text{s}$; wetted cone area: $\dfrac{4\sqrt2}{5}\text{ cm}^2/\text{s}$.
answer.worked:
Let $h$ be the water height, $r$ its surface radius and $l$ the wetted slant height, in centimetres. The semi-vertical angle gives
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{r}{h}&=\tan45^\circ=1\\r&=h.\end{aligned}$$
For the volume,
$$\begin{aligned}V&=\frac13\pi r^2h\\V&=\frac13\pi h^3\\\frac{dV}{dt}&=\pi h^2\frac{dh}{dt}\\20&=\pi h^2\frac{dh}{dt}\\\frac{dh}{dt}&=\frac{20}{\pi h^2}.\end{aligned}$$
When $h=50$,
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dh}{dt}&=\frac{20}{2500\pi}\\\frac{dh}{dt}&=\frac{4}{125\pi}\text{ cm/s}.\end{aligned}$$
The water surface area is $A_1$:
$$\begin{aligned}A_1&=\pi r^2=\pi h^2\\\frac{dA_1}{dt}&=2\pi h\frac{dh}{dt}\\\frac{dA_1}{dt}&=2\pi h\times\frac{20}{\pi h^2}\\\frac{dA_1}{dt}&=\frac{40}{h}.\end{aligned}$$
When $h=50$,
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dA_1}{dt}&=\frac{40}{50}\\\frac{dA_1}{dt}&=\frac45\text{ cm}^2/\text{s}.\end{aligned}$$
The wetted cone area is $A_2$. Since $l=\sqrt{h^2+r^2}=h\sqrt2$,
$$\begin{aligned}A_2&=\pi rl\\A_2&=\pi h^2\sqrt2\\\frac{dA_2}{dt}&=2\pi h\sqrt2\frac{dh}{dt}\\\frac{dA_2}{dt}&=2\pi h\sqrt2\times\frac{20}{\pi h^2}\\\frac{dA_2}{dt}&=\frac{40\sqrt2}{h}.\end{aligned}$$
When $h=50$,
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dA_2}{dt}&=\frac{40\sqrt2}{50}\\\frac{dA_2}{dt}&=\frac{4\sqrt2}{5}\text{ cm}^2/\text{s}.\end{aligned}$$
